# Addonry

Build and test personal Chrome and Firefox extensions.

| Maintenance | Maintained |
|---|---|
| Version | 0.3.3 |
| Clients | Codex, Claude Code, Kimi Code (legacy) |
| License | MIT |
| Source | [Repository](https://github.com/0langa/Addonry) |

Personally used and maintained as needed, without a release schedule or support guarantee.

## Example request

> Use Addonry to build a Chrome and Firefox extension that copies selected links.

## Requirements

Windows is required by the bundled Windows PowerShell launcher. Chrome and Firefox are extension targets, not supported host operating systems.

- Windows PowerShell
- Python, Node.js, and Git
- Chrome or Firefox for the extension being tested

## Install

### Codex

```shell
codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/0langa/plugins.git
codex plugin add addonry@0langas-plugins
```

### Claude Code

```shell
claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/0langa/plugins.git
claude plugin install addonry@0langas-plugins
```

## Setup and use

- Install the plugin, start a new session, then explicitly invoke Addonry. Its workflow starts only when named or invoked.
- Choose Chrome, Firefox, or both. Generated projects and ZIP packages stay local until you request publication.

## Legacy Kimi compatibility

Kimi compatibility is retained but is not actively tested. First prepare a [recursive checkout](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#development-checkout). Replace the example path with your checkout.

```text
/plugins marketplace C:\path\to\plugins\kimi-marketplace.json
/plugins install C:\path\to\plugins\plugins\addonry
/reload
```
